- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from 10-day moving avg), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) and price drops, model frequently undercorrects; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 10-day avg is > 80, forecast tends to drift down; if < 75, drifts up — adjust for 1–2% deviation from 10-day mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent sentiment; if sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.33), reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid overfitting.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is flat, model tends to predict minor moves; if true outcome shows >1% swing, increase forecast sensitivity by 1–2% to capture momentum.
